walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: postfix and circulates

steps.text: These are the same kinds of question with different values. Use the same steps on yours.
Postfix: read from the left. Push each number onto the stack.
* pops two numbers. The first one popped goes on the right: 5 * 2 = 10. Push 10.
+ pops 10, then 4: 4 + 10 = 14. One number is left on the stack. That is the value.
LCIRC-2: every bit moves 2 places left. The 2 bits that fall off the left end come back on the right.
So LCIRC-2 11010 = 01011. The string keeps its length. Now do the same with yours.

steps.label: Trick 1: Stacks and Brackets
steps.content:
Trick 1: Stacks and Brackets

Think → Pair → SharePredict the value of 6 2 4 + *. Why does postfix never need brackets?Show the worked answer

6 2 4 + * is 6 * (2 + 4) = 36. An operator always uses the two values just before it, so the order of the tokens already shows what is worked out first.

TaskThe trickExample
Postfix valueRead from the left. Push each number. An operator pops two: the first one popped goes on the right.8 2 / = 8 / 2
Prefix valueRead from the right. Push each number. An operator pops two: the first one popped goes on the left./ 8 2 = 8 / 2
Infix to postfixPut brackets round every operation. Move each operator to the end of its own brackets.(A + B) * C
A B + C *
Infix to prefixThe same, but move each operator to the front of its own brackets.(A + B) * C
* + A B C
  • ↑ is a power (type ^). It goes before * and /. 3(A + B) means 3 * (A + B).

steps.label: Trick 2: Flick Bits in the Right Order
steps.content:
Trick 2: Flick Bits in the Right Order

Think → Pair → SharePredict: what is LCIRC-5 10110? Why?Show the worked answer

10110 again. In a 5-bit string, each bit moves 5 places and wraps all the way round to where it started.

The order

  1. Brackets
  2. NOT, LSHIFT, RSHIFT, LCIRC, RCIRC: start with the one next to the bits
  3. AND
  4. XOR
  5. OR
  • Shorter string? Pad it with zeros on the left.
OperatorWhat it doesOn 10110
NOTflips every bit01001
AND, OR, XORcolumn by column: AND needs both 1, OR needs at least one 1, XOR needs them different101 AND 11011 = 00001
LSHIFT-22 bits fall off the left, 2 zeros come in on the right11000
RCIRC-11 bit falls off the right and comes back on the left01011

steps.label: Trick 3: Trace Like a Detective
steps.content:
Trick 3: Trace Like a Detective

Think → Pair → SharePredict what this program outputs. Why does p start at 1, not 0?Show the worked answer

It outputs 24: 1 * 1 * 2 * 3 * 4. Anything times 0 is 0, so a product that started at 0 would stay 0.

  • A total starts at 0 and adds a value each turn. A counter adds 1. A product starts at 1.
  • FOR i = 1 TO 9 STEP 2: i is 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. NEXT i adds the step.
  • WHILE checks its condition before every turn.
  • Nested loops: the inner loop runs all the way through for every turn of the outer loop.
  • % gives the remainder. int(x) drops the decimal part. abs(x) removes a minus sign. && means both are true.
01  p = 1
02  FOR i = 1 TO 4
03    p = p * i
04  NEXT i
05  OUTPUT p

Trace it: a column for each variable, a new row each time a value changes.
